target.title: fix(gateway-protocol): trim connect error detail codes in readConnectErrorDetailCode
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway connect-error payloads can carry padded `details.code` strings (leading/trailing whitespace). `readConnectErrorDetailCode()` previously returned the raw string after only checking `code.trim().length > 0`, so strict comparisons against `ConnectErrorDetailCodes.*` failed and downstream helpers (`readPairingConnectErrorDetails`, `formatConnectErrorMessage`) fell back to generic messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return `code.trim()` from `readConnectErrorDetailCode()` so normalized detail codes match canonical constants and structured formatting paths run for untrusted gateway error details.

## User Impact

Control UI and other gateway clients show correct pairing-required and protocol-mismatch messages when the server sends padded detail codes, instead of generic fallback text.

## Evidence

- Unit regressions in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/connect-error-details.test.ts`
- Direct oxlint on touched gateway-protocol files
- Standalone runtime proof against PR head `720115e02091e375b8b84be96842878dbe685458` showing padded detail codes normalize before pairing/protocol formatting

## Real behavior proof

### Standalone runtime proof

This runs outside Vitest and imports the PR-head gateway-protocol runtime module directly.

Command:

```
node --import tsx %TEMP%\openclaw-pr99555-proof.mjs
```

Output:

```json
}
```

target.title: fix(clickclack): wrap websocket message rejections with Error for diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack gateway WebSocket message handling could wrap non-`Error` async rejections with lossy stringification, reducing the diagnostic value of structured rejection values.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway rejection wrapper now uses `formatErrorMessage(e)` so non-`Error` values are rendered consistently with JSON-safe diagnostics while preserving the original value as the `cause`.

The regression test now drives the real `startClickClackGatewayAccount()` WebSocket `message.created` path instead of copying the local catch expression in isolation.

## User Impact

ClickClack gateway failures from structured non-`Error` rejections keep useful details in the thrown `Error` message while retaining the original rejection value for debugging.

## Evidence

- `openclaw/clickclack` dev-bootstrap service on `http://127.0.0.1:18080`: created a real workspace/channel and bot token, then drove a real HTTP message into the real ClickClack websocket `message.created` path.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testTimeout=20000 --hookTimeout=20000`: 1 file, 6 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts`: passed.

target.title: fix(openai): bound realtime voice websocket payload at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the OpenAI realtime voice backend WebSocket could accept inbound frames up to the `ws` dependency default of 100 MiB when the provider path did not set an explicit payload cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI realtime voice bridge now passes `maxPayload: 16 * 1024 * 1024` to its backend WebSocket constructor. This is an intentional hardening cap for the provider relay path; frames above 16 MiB fail closed with WebSocket close status 1009.

## User Impact

Gateway voice sessions have a bounded inbound WebSocket frame size instead of inheriting the larger dependency default.

## Evidence

- `node --import tsx outputs/pr-99450/verify-openai-voice-ws-max-payload.mjs`: loopback proof through `buildOpenAIRealtimeVoiceProvider().createBridge()` and the realtime voice WebSocket constructor.

target.title: Reject surrogate HTML numeric entities
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTML numeric entities for surrogate code points (for example, `�`) currently decode into lone surrogate UTF-16 code units. That can make extracted markdown/text no longer well-formed UTF-16 and can break downstream serialization/encoding paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`decodeCodePoint()` now rejects surrogate code points in addition to malformed, negative, and out-of-range values. Invalid numeric entities continue to be preserved literally, while valid BMP and astral code points still decode normally.

## User Impact

Fetched or syntax-highlighted HTML that contains malformed surrogate numeric entities remains stable literal text instead of introducing invalid lone surrogates. Existing valid entity decoding behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/web-fetch-utils.test.ts`
- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/web-fetch-utils.test.ts src/agents/utils/syntax-highlight.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check src/agents/utils/html.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch-utils.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Real behavior proof from the PR branch using the web_fetch extraction runtime path (`extractBasicHtmlContent`):

```text
{"text":"bad � end\ndecimal �\nlow �\nemoji 😀"}
literalHex=true
literalDecimal=true

```

The proof shows surrogate entities stay literal, the valid astral entity still decodes, and `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on the extracted text.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #24196.

Discord API allows up to 10 file attachments per message, but the integration only supported a single `mediaUrl`.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `mediaUrls?: string[]` to `DiscordSendOpts`. Auto-batches >10 files across multiple messages. Reply reference only on first batch.
2. **sendDiscordMedia** (`send.shared.ts`): Accepts `mediaUrls: string[]` — iterates all URLs into a single `files` array for Discord's multipart upload.
3. **outbound-payload.ts**: Multiple media URLs batch into one `sendMessageDiscord` call. Component messages reject multiple attachments with a clear error.
4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.
5. **Tests**: 57/57 pass. Coverage for 3-file batch, >10 auto-split with replyTo behavior, legacy backward compatibility.

## Evidence

target.title: Recover stranded message-tool finals by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85714 for the direct/source-channel failure where an agent turn can finish successfully with a substantive final answer, but the user sees nothing because the channel is in `message_tool_only` visible-reply mode and the model skipped `message(action=send)`.

This supersedes #88992. I kept the useful shape from that PR: substantive-final detection, room-event and send-policy guards, a one-shot retry marker, message-tool retry, collect isolation, deferred drain, QA coverage, and clearer prompt wording. The replacement removes the new `messages.strandedReplyRecovery` opt-in surface so guarded recovery is the default for the specific stranded-final class.

## Why This Change Was Made

The July 3 Telegram repro is not a broad final-fallback problem; it is a silent-success problem. In `message_tool_only`, final assistant text is intentionally private, but a substantive final with no message-tool delivery should not end the user-visible source turn as if everything succeeded.

The fix now:

- warns only through the existing substantive private-final predicate;
- skips `room_event`, `sendPolicyDenied`, successful source delivery, short/silent finals, and explicit silence;
- enqueues exactly one retry marked `stranded-reply-retry`;
- applies that recovery to both direct source turns and queued followup turns;
- prepends that retry ahead of already queued follow-ups, protects it from old-item overflow eviction, drains it before overflow summaries, and uses the refreshed follow-up runner;
- stores retry identity in private queued-run metadata rather than user-controlled summary text;
- forces that retry out of collect batching and suppresses retry prompt persistence;
- asks the model to deliver the sanitized visible reply via `message(action=send)`;
- if enqueueing fails or the retry strands again, delivers only a marked sanitized diagnostic;
- suppresses that diagnostic only when the retry already delivered to the source chat through the message tool or internal source-reply path;
- never marks or auto-delivers the original private final text.

## User Impact

For users in Telegram/source-channel chats configured for tool-only visible replies, a substantive reply that previously disappeared should now either:

- recover through one visible `message(action=send)` retry, or
- show `I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again.`

Intentional silence remains silent. Hidden reasoning, tool output, trace text, raw private finals, send-policy-denied text, room events, and short notes are not auto-published.

target.title: fix(exec): avoid splitting surrogate pairs in approval display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approval command display text is part of the security decision UI. The sanitizer already handles invisible Unicode characters by full code point, but its final display cap used raw `String.prototype.slice`. If the 16 KiB cap lands between the high and low surrogate of a supplementary-plane character, the approval preview can contain malformed UTF-16 such as a dangling `\uD83D` before `…[truncated]`.

That can make the command text rendered in approval prompts differ at the character level from the sanitized string the code intended to show, and can break downstream UI/payload encoding for the approval prompt.

## Summary

- Use the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper for exec approval command display output caps.
- Preserve the existing 16 KiB display cap, truncation marker, redaction-before-truncation ordering, and hard oversized-input suppression behavior.
- Add a regression test for a command whose emoji surrogate pair crosses the display truncation boundary.

## Evidence

- Runtime proof using `"a".repeat(16 * 1024 - 1) + "😀tail"` returned `{ "truncated": true, "hasLoneSurrogate": false, "encodable": true, "tail": "aaaaaaaaaaaa…[truncated]" }`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.test.ts` exited 0.
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.test.ts` reported 1 file passed / 33 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.test.ts` exited 0. Local pnpm emitted the existing Node engine warning because the machine is on Node v22.17.0 while package metadata asks for >=22.19.0.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.test.ts` exited 0.
- `git diff --check` exited 0.

## Risk

Low. This only changes the existing display truncation boundary to back off from split surrogate pairs. It does not change redaction patterns, the display size constant, the truncation marker, warning/command marker strings, or the hard input cap behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99286 — macOS dashboard Web UI: deleting a selected session does nothing and no confirmation dialog appears.

**Root cause:** The macOS `DashboardWindowController` uses WKWebView to display the Control UI, but was missing the `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` `WKUIDelegate` method. ## Why This Change Was Made

The sessions table only had a bulk-bar delete action (select checkbox → click "Delete selected"), with no per-session delete button. The bulk-bar relied on `window.confirm()` which didn't work in the embedded macOS WKWebView.

4. **CSS** — Added `.session-actions-cell` flex layout and delete button icon sizing.

target.title: fix(discord): guard message-tool-only final delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.
- Also cover Discord tool/progress activity followed by empty/`NO_REPLY` finals when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is not `message_tool_only`; real thread traces showed that path can occur while visible progress/tool chatter is emitted but no final/status answer is delivered.
- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;
  - keep unaddressed group/channel silence quiet when empty replies are allowed.

## Related context

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

- #84022 — current Discord transcript-only/suppressed final class.
- #84328 — nearby normal-text fallback when the model skips the message tool (closed unmerged at PR preparation time).
- #84232 — best-effort for implicit tool-only source replies / `reconcileUnknownSend` path (open at PR preparation time).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Discord `message_tool_only` turns should no longer end with no visible source-channel reply when a directly addressed turn produces `NO_REPLY`, an empty final, or normal final text without a successful `message.send`.
- **Real setup tested**: Real OpenClaw deployment on Linux/arm64, installed package `OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)`, with the same runtime-guard logic from this PR ported to the installed compiled runtime. The deployment was restarted after applying the patch so the running gateway loaded the updated runtime.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) accumulates an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** path was left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

This is the **only first-party Ollama native streaming consumer**. Capping here is the highest-leverage place to bound the surface — one change protects every native Ollama chat / tool-call / cloud auth flow that goes through `parseNdjsonStream`, including future maintainer changes that add NDJSON consumers downstream of this helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama bound):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call flows keep working — the only new failure mode is `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing, which is the desired safety behavior.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (3 tests in `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts`)

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

All 105 tests in `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` pass: `Tests 105 passed (105)`.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for Ollama native streaming success body (16 MiB cap + reader cancellation on overflow).
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test.
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response streams >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
7 files changed, 206 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — auto-regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen --write`
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` — +1 row
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block; signature widening is type-only)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — +177 LoC (3 inline tests + Layer 3 loopback + quantitative read-out)

## Verification

- `pnpm tsgo` — typecheck passes (core + extensions)
- `pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts --run` — 105/105 tests pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json <all 4 modified files>` — 0 lint errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` — local-only repro script passes
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passes
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` — passes (regenerated exports match entrypoints list)

## Closes / siblings

- Closes the symmetric success-body gap to `OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (8 KiB error-body bound, existing).
- Same 16 MiB cap as #95218, #95420, #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #96920, #96984, #97535, #97620, #97628 (all canonical streaming success-body bounded-read PRs).
- First extension consumer of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Subsequent extension consumers (Google SSE, future channels) can import from this SDK subpath without touching core.
- Companion SDK promotion commit bundles the helper re-export, entrypoints registration, exports sync, baseline hash regen, and docs row in one cohesive change — no consumer breaks if this PR is reverted, since the SDK seam is gated by the bound consumer in commit 2.

target.title: fix(ios): defer QR pairing after scanner dismissal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

The iOS QR scanner can crash after scanning a gateway pairing QR because the scanner delegate immediately starts gateway connection/trust UI while VisionKit is still dismissing the scanner and stopping camera capture. On device this aborts in UIKit alert presentation (`UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController`) with VisionKit concurrently stopping `AVCaptureSession`.

This PR makes onboarding and Settings QR flows queue scanned gateway links/setup codes, dismiss the scanner sheet first, then process the queued result after a short main-actor delay.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on Polly's iPhone with current-main proof build `2026.6.11 / 488`.
- Crash log: `OpenClaw-2026-07-03-160229.ips`, app bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`.
- Crash signature: `EXC_CRASH` / `SIGABRT`, `+[UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController:]`, with VisionKit stopping `AVCaptureSession` on `com.apple.visionkit.avcapturequeue`.
- Installed local patched build on the same iPhone.
- Scanned a fresh QR through onboarding/Gateway Settings; pairing completed and created an approved iPhone entry from `100.126.168.10`.
- No new QR scanner crash surfaced during the post-scan watch window.

## Implementation

- Queue scanned gateway links/setup codes in onboarding and Settings.
- Dismiss the scanner sheet before starting connection/trust UI.
- Process the queued result after a short main-actor delay.
- Cancel pending scanner continuation work when the view disappears.

## Validation

- `pnpm native:i18n:check`
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat apps/ios/Sources/Onboarding/OnboardingWizardView.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTab.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabActions.swift`
- `swiftlint lint --config apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml apps/ios/Sources/Onboarding/OnboardingWizardView.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTab.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabActions.swift`

- Simulator compile: `xcodebuild -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData-qrscanner-sim build`

target.title: fix(heartbeat): inject Slack interaction value into heartbeat prompt\…
target.body:
Fixes #99544

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99544 (follow-up to #61502). Slack interactive button clicks wake the target session and thread, but the clicked action's `value` / `action_id` never reaches the agent as input. `consumeSelectedSystemEventEntries` removes the interaction entry from the system event queue, yet the event text was never injected into the heartbeat prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat runner's prompt resolution has dedicated builders for exec-completion and cron events, but the generic fallback path never includes system event text. When a Slack hook wake triggers a heartbeat with no exec/cron events, the generic heartbeat prompt is used and the interaction payload is silently dropped.

This change adds a Slack-interaction-typed branch:

- `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts`: add `isSlackInteractionEvent()` and `buildSlackInteractionEventPrompt()`
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`: route pending system events whose `contextKey` starts with `slack:interaction:` to the new builder, mirroring the exec/cron branches

Unlike a generic "prepend all system event text" approach, this only touches events explicitly queued as Slack interactions, so it does not widen the prompt-injection surface for arbitrary system events.

The prompt builder renders **all** queued Slack interactions (with a cap of 5 rendered entries plus an overflow summary), preserving symmetry with `selectSystemEventsConsumedByHeartbeat` so no interaction is consumed without being rendered.

## User Impact

Users clicking Slack interactive buttons will see the `action_id` and `value` reflected in the agent's heartbeat turn, including multiple rapid clicks coalesced into a single wake. No other heartbeat behavior changes.

## Evidence

Unit tests:

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.test.ts

 ✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.test.ts (53 tests) 16ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  53 passed (53)
```

Integration tests (covers the multi-interaction render/consume symmetry raised by reviewer):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.slack-interaction.test.ts

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/heartbeat-runner.slack-interaction.test.ts (4 tests) 42ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Regression check on existing heartbeat runner tests:

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts (43 tests) 552ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
```

Format / lint:

```bash
$ npx oxfmt --check src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.test.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.slack-interaction.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ npx oxlint@latest src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.test.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.slack-interaction.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

Key assertions from the integration test show the prompt body contains both interactions when two are queued:

```
Slack interactive button(s) were clicked:
1. action_id="approve_pr" with value="merge-99544"
2. action_id="reject_pr" with value="close-99544"

Please act on these interaction(s). Reply HEARTBEAT_OK.
```

## Summary
- Preserve the numeric `agents.defaults.llm.idleTimeoutSeconds` value in `doctor --fix` output instead of silently dropping it.
- Add a one-shot config-load warning when `agents.defaults.llm` is still present, pointing users to `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds`.
- Cover doctor migration, partial-validation migration, and config-load diagnostics with focused tests.

Fixes #74910

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Legacy `agents.defaults.llm.idleTimeoutSeconds` was removed by `doctor --fix` with only a generic message, so users lost the old timeout value and had no actionable provider-specific migration hint.

**Real environment tested:** Local macOS OpenClaw checkout at `82e9c03`, run with isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The temp config contained `agents.defaults.llm.idleTimeoutSeconds: 180` and `models.providers.mlx`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```sh
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state pnpm openclaw health
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state pnpm openclaw doctor --fix
```

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live terminal output from the real CLI run:
```text
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state pnpm openclaw health
Config invalid
Problem:
  - agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "llm"
```

target.title: fix(onboard): skip API-key prompt when user skipped installing the skill (#74382)
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** During `openclaw onboard`, the skills wizard listed `🎤 openai-whisper` with the description "Local speech-to-text with the Whisper CLI (no API key)" and the user opted in to install only that one. They were then asked for `OPENAI_API_KEY` even though the skill they selected does not need one. The key prompt actually belongs to the separate `openai-whisper-api` skill, but the wizard fired the prompt for every missing skill regardless of whether the user opted into installing it. Reported as #74382.
- **Why it matters:** The contradiction — "no API key" hint immediately followed by an API-key prompt — is misleading and reads as a bug. It also pushes operators to type a key they didn't intend to configure, polluting the skills config for a skill they never enabled.
- **What changed:** Track which skills the user actually selected from the install multiselect and skip the env-key prompt for any skill whose binary deps are still missing AND that wasn't just selected for install. Skills that are env-only (no missing bins) still prompt as before. Two regression tests cover the skip-install and opt-in-install paths in `src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** No skill manifest changes, no install logic changes, no UX for env-only skills.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #74382
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The post-install env-key loop in `src/commands/onboard-skills.ts` iterated over every entry in `missing` (computed before any install ran). Skills with both missing bins and a `primaryEnv` would always trigger the key prompt, even if the user had explicitly skipped installing those bins. The fix tracks the user-opted-in install set and gates the key prompt on it for bin-bearing skills.

## Test Plan

- `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts` — 4/4 pass (2 existing + 2 new):
  - new: does not prompt for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when only the local `openai-whisper` (no key) was selected.
  - new: still prompts for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when `openai-whisper-api` was selected.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — clean.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all relevant lanes green; the only failure is a pre-existing `lint:core` oxlint config drift on `origin/main` (`Rule 'no-underscore-dangle' not found in plugin 'eslint'`), reproducible with no working changes.

## Real behavior proof

target.title: Add per-session runtime envelopes
target.body:
Refs #74632

## Summary

- add an optional `envelope` object to `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch`
- persist the envelope on `SessionEntry`, with `sessions.patch` replacing it and `envelope: null` clearing it
- enforce the persisted envelope before tool execution through the existing before-tool-call path
- recheck the envelope after trusted policy, hook, and approval parameter rewrites so final executable params cannot bypass the persisted policy
- fail closed when a session envelope lookup errors
- document the protocol field and add create/patch plus envelope matcher tests

The enforcement is intentionally declarative and additive:

- `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools` are matched against normalized tool names
- `allowedPaths` / `deniedPaths` are applied to common path-like tool params
- `bashCommandAllowlist` applies to common command params

This PR intentionally does not expose `networkAccess` / host allowlists. Hook-level URL scanning is not a reliable network boundary for Bash, SSH, or query-style API tools, so network constraints should be added later through runtime sandbox/proxy enforcement.

## Tests

target.title: feat(bootstrap): support session-scoped extra files
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `bootstrap-extra-files` could only apply one global extra file set, and explicitly configured extra files were still constrained by the default bootstrap basename list.
- Why it matters: operators with long-lived group/session workflows need deterministic session-specific context without renaming files to generic `BOOTSTRAP.md` or mixing unrelated domain context into shared bootstrap files.
- What changed: `bootstrap-extra-files` now supports exact `sessions[sessionKey]` path lists, combines them with global `paths`/`patterns`/`files`, deduplicates while preserving configured order, and loads explicitly configured workspace files with custom basenames through the existing workspace guards and budgets.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add channel-wide selectors, session-type selectors, tiered bootstrap policy, symlink expansion beyond existing boundary checks, or a new global `agents.defaults` schema.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #39120
- Related #73917
- Related #50876
- Related #61001
- Related #22438
- Related #22439
- Related #54315
- Related #62110
- Related #73401
- Related #73988
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

N/A

- Root cause: N/A
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A
- Contributing context (if known): Existing `bootstrap-extra-files` already resolved configured workspace paths, but the public contract only supported one global list. The basename allowlist also made explicit custom files such as `BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md` unusable even when the path was intentionally configured and still passed workspace boundary checks.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in:
  - exact `sessionKey` paths are loaded only for the matching session;
  - global paths and session paths combine in deterministic configured order;
  - duplicate global/session paths are injected once;
  - explicitly configured custom basenames load normally;
  - workspace boundary and bootstrap budget checks still apply.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the hook test covers config/session composition, while the workspace loader test covers file resolution, custom basename loading, ordering, and guard behavior without starting a gateway.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing hook tests covered global extra file injection and subagent filtering; this PR extends that coverage for session-scoped paths.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`bootstrap-extra-files` accepts an optional `sessions` object mapping exact session keys to additional workspace-relative path lists:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "internal": {
      "entries": {
        "bootstrap-extra-files": {
          "enabled": true,
          "paths": ["shared/BOOTSTRAP.md"],
          "sessions": {
            "agent:main:whatsapp:group:123": [
              "groups/support/BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md"
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Global `paths` / `patterns` / `files` remain backward compatible. Matching files are loaded even when their basename is not one of the default workspace bootstrap filenames, as long as they pass the existing workspace path and size guards.

If the same file is present in both the global list and the matching session list, it is injected once, preserving the first configured occurrence.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[agent:bootstrap] -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths only] -> [same extras in every session]

After:
[agent:bootstrap]
  -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths]
  -> [exact sessions[sessionKey] paths when configured]
  -> [dedupe + workspace guards + session bootstrap filter]
  -> [session-specific context]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

Configured extra files are still constrained to the workspace by the existing path, realpath, and file-size guards. This PR does not add external path access or expand tool execution.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / local pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A


### Steps

1. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.paths` with a global extra file.
2. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.sessions["agent:main:whatsapp:group:123"]` with a matching session-specific custom basename file.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** exact-session `bootstrap-extra-files.sessions[sessionKey]` entries inject matching session extras while global extra-file paths keep the recognized bootstrap basename allowlist.

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that command:


What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios:

Existing `bootstrap-extra-files.paths`, `patterns`, and `files` configs continue to work. Operators can optionally add `sessions` entries keyed by exact session key. No migration is required.

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: config: accept per-agent elevatedDefault overrides and complete per-agent verbose/elevated flow (#73680)
target.body:
## Summary

Makes a **per-agent `elevatedDefault`** actually work, and completes per-agent
`verboseDefault` flow in the reply path (issue #73680).

## The gap

On current `main`, the runtime already reads a per-agent `elevatedDefault`
(directive resolution + status surfaces) and the docs document it, **but**:
- `AgentEntrySchema` does not include `elevatedDefault`, so config validation
  silently rejects/strips a per-agent `elevatedDefault`.
- `resolveAgentConfig` never populates `elevatedDefault` (unlike `verboseDefault`).
- The reply directive resolution reads only `agentCfg.elevatedDefault` (the global
  default) and `agentCfg.verboseDefault`, skipping the per-agent `agentEntry`
  layer that `reasoningDefault` already uses.

Net effect: a documented per-agent `elevatedDefault` had no effect.

## The fix

- Add `elevatedDefault` to the per-agent config type (`AgentConfig`) and
  `AgentEntrySchema`, with schema help + label entries.
- Resolve it in `resolveAgentConfig` as `entry.elevatedDefault ?? defaults.elevatedDefault`,
  mirroring `verboseDefault`.
- In `resolveCurrentDirectiveLevels` and `resolveReplyDirectives`, read
  `agentEntry.elevatedDefault` (and `agentEntry.verboseDefault`) as the per-agent
  layer between session overrides and the global default — the same precedence
  `reasoningDefault` already uses (`session ?? agentEntry ?? global`). Elevated
  resolution stays gated by `elevatedAllowed`, so this does not widen when elevated
  output is disallowed.
- Regenerate the config doc baseline hash for the new key.

`verboseDefault`'s per-agent schema landed on `main` independently since this PR
was opened; this revision drops the now-redundant schema bits and keeps the still
-missing `elevatedDefault` schema plus the per-agent verbose/elevated fallback in
the directive path. Rebased onto current `main`.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.levels.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` → 46 passed (new: per-agent elevated resolution, directive precedence session > agent > global, schema acceptance).
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` → OK.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` → clean. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.

Closes #73680

target.title: feat(openai): add queryTask/documentTask config for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings
target.body:
## Summary

Add typed `queryTask` and `documentTask` configuration under `agents.*.memorySearch` for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings through the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

Closes #74419

## Background

Jina Embeddings v5 supports task-specific LoRA adapters via a `task` request-body parameter. Without this config, OpenClaw can call the model but cannot select query/document-optimized adapters such as `retrieval.query` and `retrieval.passage`.

## Changes

- Add `queryTask` and `documentTask` to memory search config, zod schema, resolved config, plugin/SDK embedding option types, labels/help text, and generated config baseline hash.
- Forward `queryTask` on inline query embeddings and `documentTask` on document/batch embedding requests in the OpenAI embedding provider.
- Include `documentTask` in OpenAI batch embedding cache identity.
- Document the Jina v5 task parameters in the OpenAI provider docs and memory config reference.
- Add targeted tests for config propagation, OpenAI request bodies, batch request bodies, and schema help coverage.

## Supported task values

- `retrieval.query` / `retrieval.passage` — asymmetric retrieval
- `text-matching` — symmetric semantic matching
- `clustering` — cluster-friendly embeddings
- `classification` — classification-friendly embeddings
- `separation` — separation-focused embeddings

When left unset, Jina v5 defaults to general-purpose embeddings.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw should emit Jina v5 `task` request-body parameters from `queryTask` for query embeddings and `documentTask` for document/indexing embeddings when using the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on Linux/Node 22, running the actual `extensions/openai/embedding-provider.ts` code against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP capture server. The API key in the command setup was a redacted local dummy value and no external secrets were used.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** Ran `node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs`. The script started a local `/v1/embeddings` capture server, created the OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider with `model: "jina-embeddings-v3"`, `queryTask: "retrieval.query"`, and `documentTask: "retrieval.passage"`, then called `provider.embedQuery("query text")` and `provider.embedBatch(["document text"])`.

**Evidence after fix:** Live terminal output from the run:

```bash
$ node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs
{
  "setup": "local OpenAI-compatible capture server + OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider",
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "query text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.query"
      }
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/v1/embeddings",
      "body": {
        "model": "jina-embeddings-v3",
        "input": [
          "document text"
        ],
        "task": "retrieval.passage"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The captured OpenClaw-generated query embedding request included `task: "retrieval.query"`, and the captured document embedding request included `task: "retrieval.passage"`. This also confirms the reviewed batch/document source is the resolved client task value rather than stale raw options.

**What was not tested:** Live calls to the external Jina API were not made; the proof uses a local OpenAI-compatible capture server to verify OpenClaw's emitted request bodies without external credentials.

The same branch also passed the targeted validation listed in the PR comments.

target.title: fix(agent): classify stuck recovery as idle timeout
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Fixes #93610. Diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborted active embedded runs with the same downstream semantics as user/restart/superseded aborts, so failover could see an external abort and surface `Request was aborted` instead of using the configured idle-timeout fallback path.
- Why it matters / User impact: Cron/provider sessions that stall while a model call is actively in flight can use the existing idle-timeout rotate/fallback path, while stale post-model recoveries and side-effecting tool stalls stay out of automatic replay paths.
- Solution: Preserve `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and reply-run propagation, then classify replay safety from active model-call state and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics.
- Current-head refresh: re-ran production-module runtime proof, focused Vitest shards, changed-file oxlint, whitespace check, and CI failure attribution on current PR head `cc8b872ec42568fcee945e815c886d6d346d2495`.
- Fixes #93610

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic stuck-session recovery needs different downstream semantics depending on what was active when recovery fired. A stalled model call can safely use the existing idle-timeout fallback path; an active potential-side-effect tool call must not be replayed; stale or unknown recovery should remain external-abort-like.

## User Impact

Users running scheduled or provider-backed embedded-agent sessions get a safer recovery path when the stuck-session watchdog interrupts an active model call. The patch avoids widening retry behavior for side-effecting tool execution, so recovery does not silently replay operations that may already have touched external state.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent downstream recovery classification hardening. Provider-boundary PRs such as #93965 are related to the original opencode-go stream outage, but this PR covers the generic downstream diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **#93965:** Provider-owned opencode-go stream guard. It addresses the upstream provider stream boundary and formally closed the original issue. This PR does not replace it.
- **#93640:** Earlier provider-scoped stalled stream guard. It overlaps the provider-boundary direction and remains separate from this downstream recovery classification boundary.
- **#98580:** Adjacent timeout-budget work for cron stuck recovery. Landing order should be deliberate because it can affect when recovery fires, but this PR still owns what happens after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run.
- **This PR:** Downstream embedded-run recovery safety. It fixes the boundary after diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborts an active embedded run: `stuck_recovery` must survive registry/reply-run propagation, and replay safety must be classified before failover decides whether retry/fallback is allowed.
- **Why this can still land alongside provider/timeout-budget fixes:** Even with provider-owned stream termination guards or timeout-budget changes, the generic stuck-session recovery path still needs replay-safe semantics for model stalls, side-effecting tool stalls, and stale recovery.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:**
```text
Diagnostic stuck-session recovery preserves `stuck_recovery` through embedded-run and reply-run boundaries, then classifies replay safety before failover observes abort semantics:
- active model-call stall with no active potential-side-effect tool => model_idle_timeout, eligible for the existing rotate/fallback path;
- active side-effecting tool stall => tool_execution_timeout, not idle timeout, so failover does not replay side effects;
- stale post-model / pre-model / unknown stuck recovery => external_abort, not a replay path.
```

- **Real environment tested:**
```text

Evidence directory: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-93655-evidence

Current origin/main: e272da5c5579b68deee084f7e1655896a197cc94

A production-module runtime probe imported the same stuck-recovery classifier, embedded-run registry, abort/drain path, and reply-run registry modules from this worktree. It registered an in-process active embedded run, aborted it with `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"`, waited for drain, and separately exercised reply-run stuck-recovery cancellation.
```

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```sh

EVIDENCE_DIR="/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-93655-evidence"
```


- **What was not tested:**
```text

The fresh proof exercises the downstream OpenClaw diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary on the current PR head. Provider-owned stream termination behavior remains covered by provider-boundary PRs and is not claimed as live provider proof here.
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for the downstream diagnostic recovery / embedded-run failover classification boundary; complementary to provider-owned stream guard fixes.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 — runtime/live classification proof:** Addressed with current-head production-module runtime proof showing model-call stuck recovery => `model_idle_timeout`, side-effecting tool stuck recovery => `tool_execution_timeout`, and stale/unknown recovery => `external_abort`.
- **RF-002 — owner replay-safety confirmation:** Contributor proof is supplied, but final agent/session-owner sign-off remains a maintainer decision before merge.
- **RF-003 — after-fix real behavior proof:** Addressed with terminal runtime-harness output in `current-head-stuck-recovery-runtime-proof-20260703.json`, plus current-head focused tests.
- **RF-004 — intentional session recovery semantic change:** Disclosed as intentional and bounded: only active model-call stalls without active potential-side-effect tools enter model idle-timeout fallback semantics.
- **RF-005 — active side-effect counter boundary:** Covered by focused tests and runtime classification; final owner confirmation of the exact replay-safety boundary remains a maintainer decision.
- **RF-006 — original opencode-go outage proof gap:** Disclosed explicitly. This PR proves the downstream recovery boundary; it does not claim a live opencode-go provider outage reproduction.
- **RF-007 — adjacent #98580 timeout-budget work:** Disclosed in the linked PR analysis. That work can affect when recovery fires; this PR owns how recovery is classified after it fires.

target.title: docs(gateway): add external auth-proxy recipe
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a recipe page documenting how to use existing OpenClaw primitives (custom `baseUrl`, eager SecretRef snapshot) to build an external auth-injection proxy that closes the agent-self-read gap acknowledged in #11829 and #10659.

The page does **not** propose any core change. It documents a pattern users can apply today.

## Why now

`@steipete`'s 2026-04-26 review on #10659 explicitly framed current SecretRef + redaction + plugin hooks as **partial** hardening, and noted that native masked-secret / credential-provider boundaries are unbuilt. PR #9271 attempted a full in-core proxy and was closed unmerged at 15.9K LOC. PRs #12839 and #22744 followed similar fates.

That leaves users hitting this issue with no documented workaround. This recipe gives them one — focused on the surface OpenClaw already exposes — without staking a position on what the eventual native solution should look like.

## Field validation

Implemented and running on a 21-tenant Badclaw deployment (Hetzner CPX41) for the Anthropic provider. End-to-end verification:

- Agent container has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, in `/run/secrets/`, or anywhere on its filesystem.
- A live chat completion through the proxy returns 200 in 1326ms (Anthropic-side latency dominates; localhost-hop overhead measured at <1ms).
- Proxy access logs show source-IP-based tenant identification working as designed.

Reference implementation linked from the page: https://github.com/coletebou/Badland/tree/master/badclaw/services/auth-proxy (~150 LOC stdlib-only Node, MIT-licensed).

## What this PR doesn't do

- Doesn't add a built-in proxy. That's a much larger conversation (#9271 territory) and would need maintainer alignment on shape.
- Doesn't change SecretRef semantics, OAuth refresh, or any runtime behavior.
- Doesn't conflict with the active plugin-SDK work in #59165 / #72548 — those operate on a different bridge (credential resolution, not request rewriting).

## Test plan

- [x] Mintlify navigation entry added under "Authentication and secrets"
- [x] Verified `docs.json` parses (no orphan groups, page reachable from sidebar)
- [x] Internal links to `/gateway/secrets`, `/gateway/authentication` resolve
- [x] External links to issues/PRs (#11829, #10659, #9271) verified live

## Related

- #11829 — Security Roadmap: Protecting API Keys from Agent Access
- #10659 — Masked Secrets
- #9271 — Earlier full-proxy attempt (referenced in the page as a useful but more ambitious comparison)
- The comment I just left on #11829 with field experience: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/11829#issuecomment-4342619242
