target.title: fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank
target.body:
**PR title:** `fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank`

---

## Summary

- **Problem:** `openclaw logs --follow` prints `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` to stderr whenever the gateway log grows faster than `--max-bytes` between polls, even though no rotation has occurred — the cursor is still valid and the tail was just truncated to fit the byte budget.
- **Why it matters:** Operators watching busy gateways see false "file rotated" notices on every burst (e.g. during a noisy startup or while a chatty channel pumps logs). The accompanying `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` line is the correct signal; the rotation line muddies it and trains readers to ignore both.
- **What changed:** In `src/logging/log-tail.ts::readLogSlice`, only set `reset = true` in the true rotation case (`cursor > size` — the file shrank below the previous cursor). The fast-growth branch (`size - start > maxBytes`) now sets `truncated = true` only, since the cursor it returned remains contiguous with what the caller saw last poll.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** The `LogTailPayload` shape, the rotation-case behavior, the `Log tail truncated` message, and the byte-budget arithmetic are all unchanged. No CLI strings, schema, or downstream consumers were modified — `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts` and `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` continue to work with the same fields.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration *(logging is shared infra)*
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX *(stderr notice text)*
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- No existing issue. Found while reading sibling cron handler code around #74066.
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- **Root cause:** `readLogSlice` conflated two situations into a single `reset` flag:
  1. `cursor > size` — the previously-returned cursor is past EOF; the file was rotated/truncated, so the cursor is meaningless and we must restart from the new tail.
  2. `size - start > maxBytes` — the file grew faster than the per-poll byte budget; the cursor is still valid, we just can't read everything that was appended in one poll.
  Only case (1) is a real reset/rotation. Case (2) was incorrectly being flagged as "rotated" because both branches set `reset = true`.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** `log-tail.test.ts` only covered the redaction path; nothing pinned the meaning of `reset` vs `truncated`.
- **Contributing context:** The CLI side (`src/cli/logs-cli.ts:402`) hard-codes `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` for `payload.reset`, so the conflation surfaced as a misleading user-visible string rather than a silent boolean.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file:** `src/logging/log-tail.test.ts`
- **Scenarios the test locks in:**
  1. File grows by `>> maxBytes` between two polls with the same valid cursor → `truncated: true`, `reset: false`, lines returned.
  2. File shrinks below the previous cursor (real rotation) → `reset: true`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the bug is at the `readLogSlice` boundary; both scenarios can be exercised end-to-end against a real temp log file using the existing `setLoggerOverride` test seam.
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any):** none.
- **If no new test is added, why not:** N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`openclaw logs --follow` (and JSON-mode `--json`) no longer emits the `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` notice during high-throughput writes. The existing `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` notice still fires in that case, which is the actionable signal. The notice still fires correctly when the log is genuinely rotated/truncated.

## Diagram (if applicable)

`N/A`

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`
- N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL) / Windows 11 host
- Runtime/container: Node 22 (`pnpm dev`)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A — gateway logs only
- Relevant config (redacted): default loggerSettings

### Steps (to reproduce the original misleading notice on `main`)

1. Start a gateway with anything that writes a steady stream of log lines (e.g. a chatty channel or `openclaw status --watch` against a busy gateway).
2. In another terminal: `openclaw logs --follow --max-bytes 4000`.
3. Wait for a write burst that exceeds 4 KB between two polls.

### Expected

Only `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` is printed to stderr while the burst is being caught up.

### Actual (before this PR)

Both `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` **and** `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` are printed, even though the file was never rotated.

### After this PR

Only the truthful `Log tail truncated` notice is printed during fast growth. The rotation notice still fires when the file is actually rotated/truncated (covered by the second new test).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after *(see new tests in `src/logging/log-tail.test.ts`)*
- [x] Trace/log snippets *(see "Repro + Verification")*
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Local verification:

```
# Targeted unit lane
pnpm test src/logging/log-tail.test.ts
# Expect: 3 tests pass (1 existing + 2 new)
```

> Note: I was unable to run the full repository test sweep locally (the dev environment is on a WSL/Windows-mounted filesystem that pnpm refuses to install into with `ERR_PNPM_EACCES`). The fix is a 5-line local change inside `readLogSlice` with no schema, no public-API, and no other call-site impact, and the new tests exercise the exact two paths affected. CI in this repo runs the full lane.

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios:** fast file growth between polls → no rotation message; real rotation (file shrunk) → rotation message still emitted.
- **Edge cases checked:** initial poll with no cursor still uses `start = max(0, size - maxBytes)` and reports `truncated` only (unchanged); empty file still returns `cursor: size, lines: []` (unchanged); cursor inside `[start, size]` window with `size - start <= maxBytes` is unchanged.
- **What I did NOT verify:** live CLI output against a running daemon during a real burst (will rely on CI + reviewer spot-check).

## Review Conversations

- [x] I will reply to or resolve every bot review conversation I address in this PR.
- [x] I will leave unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`
- N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** a downstream consumer relies on `reset === true` to mean "skipped some lines" rather than "the cursor is no longer meaningful".
  - **Mitigation:** I grepped the repo for `payload.reset` / `LogTailPayload`. The only consumers are `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` (renders the user-visible string this PR is correcting) and `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts::sanitizeLogTail` (passes the boolean through verbatim into the support bundle). Both are display-only; neither uses `reset` to decide whether lines were skipped — they use the existing `truncated` flag for that.

---

## AI/Vibe-Coded PRs Welcome! 🤖

- [x] **AI-assisted PR.** Drafted with help from Claude (Opus 4.7) via the GitHub Copilot CLI agent harness.
- [x] **Degree of testing:** lightly tested — new unit tests added; full repo lane not run locally (see note above).
- [x] **Prompts/session logs:** available on request.
- [x] I understand exactly what the code does (5-line semantic narrowing of when `reset` is asserted in `readLogSlice`).
- [ ] `codex review --base origin/main` not run locally (no Codex access in this environment); happy to address Codex bot comments after the PR opens.
- [x] Will resolve bot review conversations after addressing them.



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `readLogSlice` in `src/logging/log-tail.ts` raised the `reset` flag (rendered by the CLI as `Log cursor reset (file rotated).`) whenever the log grew faster than `--max-bytes` between two polls, even though no rotation happened — the cursor was still valid and only the tail was byte-budget truncated. Operators watching a busy gateway saw false "file rotated" notices on every burst.

**Real environment tested:** Local Node v22 runtime (Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL) driving the actual shipped `readConfiguredLogTail` export from this branch through `node --import tsx`, pointed at a real on-disk log file via the public `setLoggerOverride({ file })` seam. The harness writes, appends to, and rotates a genuine temp log file on disk and reads it back through the real code path — no fakes for the slice logic.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```
node --import tsx ./proof_logtail.ts
// proof_logtail.ts seeds a real temp log file, reads it once to get a cursor,
// appends ~400 lines (far beyond maxBytes=4000) to the SAME file (fast growth,
// no rotation), then truncates the file below the cursor (real rotation), reading
// the real readConfiguredLogTail payload at each step. Run against upstream/main and this branch.
```

**Evidence after fix:** Real console output captured from the command above, run first against the current upstream/main slice logic, then against this branch:
```
########## BEFORE PATCH (current upstream/main log-tail.ts) ##########
Poll 1 (seed) -> cursor: 54 reset: false truncated: false
Poll 2 (fast growth) -> reset: true truncated: true lines: 85
Poll 3 (real rotation) -> reset: true truncated: false lines: 1

########## AFTER PATCH (this branch log-tail.ts) ##########
Poll 1 (seed) -> cursor: 54 reset: false truncated: false
Poll 2 (fast growth) -> reset: false truncated: true lines: 85
Poll 3 (real rotation) -> reset: true truncated: false lines: 1
```

**Observed result after fix:** Before the change, Poll 2 (fast growth, same file) reported `reset: true` — a false rotation signal. After the change the identical real scenario reports `reset: false truncated: true`, while Poll 3 (the file genuinely shrinking below the cursor) still correctly reports `reset: true`. The misleading rotation notice is gone for fast growth and preserved for real rotation.

**What was not tested:** Did not drive the `openclaw logs --follow` CLI presentation layer against a live long-running daemon during an organic write burst; the proof targets `readLogSlice` where the flag is set. The CLI string mapping of `reset` is unchanged by this PR.

target.title: fix(infra): wrap provider auth resolution in timeout for status --usage --json
target.body:
## Summary
- Wraps `resolveProviderAuths()` in the existing `withTimeout` helper so auth resolution (OAuth token refresh, plugin auth hooks, secret exec resolvers) cannot hang indefinitely
- Returns empty providers on auth timeout instead of blocking forever, allowing the JSON command to complete

## Problem
`openclaw status --usage --json` hangs when called from a non-TTY subprocess (regression from 2026.4.23 to 2026.4.26). The individual provider usage fetches are bounded by `withTimeout`, but `resolveProviderAuths()` — which iterates sequentially over 7 providers calling plugin auth hooks, OAuth token refresh, and secret ref resolvers — had **no timeout boundary**. In a non-TTY subprocess, any of these can block indefinitely.

## Changes

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.ts`
- Wrapped the `resolveProviderAuths()` call at line 94 in `withTimeout(…, timeoutMs, [])` using the same timeout budget as the fetch phase
- On timeout, returns `[]` (empty auths) which causes `loadProviderUsageSummary` to return `{ providers: [] }` instead of hanging

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.test.ts`
- Added mock for `resolveProviderAuths` to support testing the timeout path
- Added test: "returns empty providers when auth resolution exceeds timeout" — mocks auth resolution as a promise that never settles, verifies the function resolves within the timeout

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: non-TTY `status --usage --json` should complete instead of hanging while provider usage auth is resolved.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on branch `fix/status-json-usage-auth-timeout-74085`, head `9852b6356b6a8369bc4f9e19b71745466d6103c5`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node -e '<script uses child_process.spawnSync("node", ["scripts/run-node.mjs", "status", "--usage", "--json"], { timeout: 45000, encoding: "utf8", non-TTY stdio capture }) and prints only exit status, elapsed time, JSON parse status, top-level keys, and usage summary shape>'
```

Evidence after fix:

target.title: fix(agents): accept multi-line ANNOUNCE_SKIP on final line
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix `isAnnounceSkip()` to also accept multi-line sub-agent output where `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` appears as the final line after a newline, not just as the sole content.
- Add focused unit tests for `sessions-send-tokens.ts` covering exact, whitespace-padded, multi-line, and negative cases.
- Add an e2e regression test for the multi-line announce-skip scenario.

Closes #74071

## Problem

Sub-agents that produce a DM summary block followed by `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` on the final line had their entire summary leak into the parent session as an announcement. The strict equality check `(text ?? "").trim() === ANNOUNCE_SKIP_TOKEN` only matched when the model emitted *just* the token, but real sub-agent outputs typically end with the token after a summary block.

## Fix

`isAnnounceSkip()` now checks two conditions:
1. **Exact match** (existing): trimmed text equals the token
2. **Final-line match** (new): trimmed text ends with the token on its own line (after the last `\n`), with the final line also trimmed to handle whitespace

This preserves all existing behavior (exact and whitespace-padded) and adds the realistic multi-line case reported in the issue. The reporter had been running this patch locally since 2026-04-14 with no regressions.

## Test plan

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tokens.test.ts` — 16 new focused unit tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` — 9 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts` — 3 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` — 15 existing tests (all pass)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sub-agent output ending with a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` should suppress completion announcement delivery, while `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` followed by more text should not be treated as a silent sentinel.
Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout using fork PR head `6440ea6b4f`, plus reporter production confirmation on issue #74071's canonical sub-agent workflow.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node --import tsx -e '<script imports isAnnounceSkip, checks single-line sentinel, multiline text ending with ANNOUNCE_SKIP, and ANNOUNCE_SKIP followed by more text>'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "branch": "fork/fix/announce-skip-multiline-74071",
  "head": "6440ea6b4f",
  "command": "node --import tsx isAnnounceSkip proof",
  "cases": [
    {
      "name": "single-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 1,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "multiline final-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 3,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "sentinel not final",
      "lineCount": 2,
      "result": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix: a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` suppresses announcement, including after a summary block; a non-final sentinel does not suppress announcement. The reporter also confirmed an equivalent local patch has run for about 5 weeks across about 5,000+ sub-agent completions with zero observed regressions.
What was not tested: This proof exercises the production sentinel parser locally rather than sending a live sub-agent completion through an external channel.

## Notes

- `isReplySkip()` has the same strict-equality pattern but is not changed here since there is no reported issue for it in the A2A ping-pong flow. It could receive the same treatment in a follow-up if needed.
- Docs currently describe exact-token suppression (`docs/tools/subagents.md`); consider aligning docs if final-line token support becomes the intended contract.

target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous, especially when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, or global Location Services were disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, and significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

## Current upstream status
Latest `origin/main` already has May embedded-runner/subagent performance work and trace logging for startup stages. It still does not expose the attempt prep stage summary to `agent_end` hook observers. This PR is narrowed to that missing diagnostics surface so plugins can collect stage timing evidence without patching core locally.

OpenClaw records detailed embedded runner prep stages internally, but that timing data is not available to plugin hooks. target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`

- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.

target.title: fix(usage): handle Daylight saving time (DST) hour boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Control UI Usage-page freeze when a long session spans a local Daylight saving time (DST) transition.

Today the hour-slicing code computes a local `:59:59.999` hour end from the current wall-clock time. In a repeated local hour at Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, that can resolve to an earlier instant and stop cursor progress.

This change switches Usage hour slicing and selected-hour filtering to monotonic next-hour-boundary stepping so aggregation always moves forward in the selected timezone.

## Why

This fixes cases where:

- Usage is rendered in local time
- a session spans a Daylight saving time (DST) fallback or spring-forward boundary
- the page builds hour buckets or applies a selected-hour filter

Without this change, the Control UI can wedge the browser main thread while rendering Usage data for long sessions.

## Changes

- replace the ambiguous local end-of-hour calculation with `getNextHourStart()` plus bounded next-hour stepping in `ui/src/ui/views/usage-metrics.ts`
- convert session hour slicing to half-open intervals `[cursor, nextBoundary)` so exact boundaries do not create zero-duration buckets
- route the selected-hour filter in `ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts` through the same DST-safe helper instead of maintaining a duplicate loop
- add focused node-side regression coverage for Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, Daylight saving time (DST) spring-forward, peak-error aggregation, and full Usage render with an hour filter

## Testing

Built and tested in: Codex App
Model: GPT-5.4
Reasoning effort: Extra High

Add AbortSignal support to batch polling loops to enable immediate cancellation when clients disconnect.

Problem
When HTTP clients disconnect during batch embedding operations, server-side polling continues until timeout, wasting API quota.

Solution
- Replace uncancelable setTimeout with cancellable version using clearTimeout
- Add signal?: AbortSignal parameter to all batch providers
- Use { once: true } to prevent listener accumulation (fixes MaxListenersExceededWarning)
- Thread signal through full call chain: batch-runner → runXxxBatches → waitForXxxBatch

Changes
- batch-runner.ts: Add signal to EmbeddingBatchExecutionParams type
- batch-openai.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup
- batch-voyage.ts: Update sleep type, add signal threading through deps
- batch-gemini.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup

Testing
- Verified polling stops within 1s of abort (was 30+ iterations)
- No listener leaks after long polls
- TypeScript compiles without errors

Backwards Compatible: signal is optional.

target.title: fix(codex): ignore missing mirrored session history
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server harness hooks can warn with `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks` when they read mirrored history before the session JSONL file exists.

Current `main` already treats parsed-empty session history as `[]`, so this PR focuses on the remaining transient state: `ENOENT` while the file-backed active transcript artifact has not been created yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing mirrored session file during startup means there is no history to replay yet. It should behave like empty history rather than surfacing as a failed history read.

Malformed non-empty history remains unchanged: the reader still returns `undefined`, so the existing warning path continues to surface real transcript corruption.

## User Impact

This reduces noisy Codex embedded-runtime warnings for healthy new sessions whose mirrored history file is created after the harness hook runs.

It does not suppress warnings for malformed non-empty transcript files.

## Evidence

- Local gateway log evidence from `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-07-03.log`: `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks` appeared for yuantai cron sessions before the corresponding JSONL file's first record timestamp; after the run completed, those files parsed successfully.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed in the rebased worktree before running validation.
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` live terminal proof passed from the patched checkout and imported the production `runCodexAppServerAttempt` path, not Vitest.
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` live terminal proof passed from the patched checkout and imported the production `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages` wrapper, not Vitest.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts` passed with `12` tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Codex harness hook history reads should not warn when the mirrored session file is temporarily missing during a new-session startup race.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw gateway logs from `2026-07-03` under the user's active `~/.openclaw` state, plus the current source checkout rebased onto `upstream/main` at `0420aefb1d` and patched through `fb7c53c51c`.

### After-fix production Codex attempt proof

This proof does not use Vitest. It runs a one-shot Node process from the patched checkout, imports the production `runCodexAppServerAttempt` implementation from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts`, starts an in-process app-server client double, and lets the real Codex attempt startup path proceed through `thread/start`, `turn/start`, and cleanup. The session file is intentionally missing before the attempt starts, matching the startup race that produced the gateway warning.

Exact post-patch command shape:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { embeddedAgentLog } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime';
import { runCodexAppServerAttempt } from './extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts';

// Create a temp workspace with a missing session.jsonl, run the production
// Codex attempt startup path with an in-process app-server client, and count
// whether the exact harness-hook warning is emitted.
EOF
```

Relevant output from the patched checkout:

```text
patched production Codex attempt proof: missing mirrored session.jsonl
  before_run_session_file_exists=no
  after_run_session_file_exists=yes
  app_server_methods=thread/start,turn/start,thread/unsubscribe
  result_keys=aborted,agentHarnessResultClassification,assistantTexts,attemptUsage,bootstrapPromptWarningSignature,bootstrapPromptWarningSignaturesSeen,cloudCodeAssistFormatError,currentAttemptAssistant,didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool,didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt,didSendViaMessagingTool,externalAbort,heartbeatToolResponse,idleTimedOut,itemLifecycle,lastAssistant,messagesSnapshot,messagingToolSentMediaUrls,messagingToolSentTargets,messagingToolSentTexts,messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads,promptError,promptErrorSource,replayMetadata,sessionIdUsed,successfulCronAdds,systemPromptReport,timedOut,timedOutDuringCompaction,timedOutDuringToolExecution,toolAudioAsVoice,toolMediaUrls,toolMetas,yieldDetected
  client_closed=no
  warning="failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks" emitted=no
  total_warn_count=0
```

What the production attempt proof verifies:

- The session JSONL is absent before the attempt starts (`before_run_session_file_exists=no`).
- The same production attempt path used by Codex embedded runtime reaches app-server startup and turn execution (`thread/start`, `turn/start`, `thread/unsubscribe`).
- The exact reported warning is not emitted while the missing session file is treated as empty history.
- The runtime creates the session file later in the turn (`after_run_session_file_exists=yes`), matching the observed startup race rather than a permanently invalid path.

### After-fix production wrapper proof

This proof does not use Vitest. It runs a one-shot Node process from the patched checkout, imports the production `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages` wrapper from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts`, and captures the production `embeddedAgentLog.warn` call site that emits `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks`.

Exact post-patch command shape:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { embeddedAgentLog } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime';

// Create a temp missing session.jsonl, call the production wrapper, and count
```

Relevant output from the patched checkout:


What the live wrapper proof verifies:

- Missing `session.jsonl` returns `[]` from the same wrapper used by harness hooks.
- `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is not called for that missing-file case, so the reported gateway warning is not emitted.
- Malformed non-empty JSONL still returns `undefined` and calls `embeddedAgentLog.warn("failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks", { sessionFile })`, preserving the real-corruption warning path.

### Regression tests

Exact post-patch test command:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts --reporter verbose
```

Relevant output:

```text
✓ |extension-codex| ../../extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts > Codex app-server attempt context > treats missing mirrored session history as empty without hook warning 5ms
✓ |extension-codex| ../../extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts > Codex app-server attempt context > keeps malformed mirrored session history on the hook warning path 2ms
✓ |extension-codex| ../../extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts > readCodexMirroredSessionHistoryMessages > treats a missing mirrored session file as empty history 1ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  12 passed (12)
```

## Related

- Follow-up to closed duplicate PR #99567. That PR covered empty/whitespace history on the old reader; current `main` already handles parsed-empty history. This PR covers the missing-file transient state against the current scoped reader API.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing chat history in Control UI / WebChat would still receive embedded `data:` image payloads on Responses-style media blocks (`input_image.image_url` and legacy `image.url`) after history sanitization, even though other base64 and data-URL media paths were already redacted.

Also fixes CI failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`: live WebChat broadcast must keep `{ type: "input_image", image_url: "data:..." }` for QR/image delivery, so inline media redaction is scoped to history-only paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock()` now treats Responses media blocks the same as existing image/audio redaction when `redactInlineMedia: true` is passed from history paths only. Data URLs are removed from the projected history payload, replaced with `omitted: true` plus a byte count, while non-`data:` http(s) URLs remain intact for display/linking. Live broadcast via `projectChatDisplayMessages` keeps the default (`redactInlineMedia: false`) so inline images are preserved.

All chat.history-style callers now opt in: main gateway (`chat.ts`), session SSE snapshots (`session-history-state.ts`), embedded gateway stub, and TUI embedded backend.

## User Impact

Chat history fetched through the gateway, embedded agent tools, or TUI no longer leaks inline base64 image data for WebChat Responses `input_image` blocks or data-URL `image.url` blocks. Operators and users still see that media was present (via `omitted` + `bytes`) without shipping the raw payload over the wire. Remote https image links continue to display normally. Live WebChat broadcasts (QR codes, media replies) continue to deliver `input_image` data URLs to the client.

## Evidence

target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

target.title: fix(ui): add per-session delete button to Control UI sessions view
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99286 — macOS dashboard Web UI: deleting a selected session does nothing and no confirmation dialog appears.

**Root cause:** The macOS `DashboardWindowController` uses WKWebView to display the Control UI, but was missing the `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` `WKUIDelegate` method. WebKit treats an unimplemented confirm-panel delegate as **Cancel**, so `window.confirm()` silently returned false and sessions could never be deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sessions table only had a bulk-bar delete action (select checkbox → click "Delete selected"), with no per-session delete button. The bulk-bar relied on `window.confirm()` which didn't work in the embedded macOS WKWebView.

## Changes

1. **Native WKUIDelegate confirm handler** — Added `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` to `DashboardWindowController.swift`, bridging `window.confirm()` to a native `NSAlert` sheet so the delete confirmation dialog works in the embedded macOS dashboard.

target.title: fix(memory-core): WAL checkpoint after writeMeta + stale index file cleanup
target.body:
## Summary

One focused fix: `writeMeta()` now runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` after writing the `memory_index_meta_v1` row, ensuring it survives process crashes.

## Problem

When the gateway process is killed between `writeMeta()` and `closeMemoryDatabase()`, the meta row exists only in the SQLite WAL file. On next startup, the manager reads no meta and declares the index "missing" — even though chunks are still present in the DB.

This puts the system into a permanent degraded state: `memory_search` returns `"index metadata is missing"`, normal syncs cannot self-heal (depending on provider availability), and the only recovery is `openclaw memory index --force`.

## Real behavior proof

Minimal reproduction using Node v24.16.0 native SQLite in WAL mode on Windows 11, with child processes killed via `taskkill /F` (SIGKILL equivalent):

```
=== WAL Meta Durability Reproduction ===

Phase 1: Normal close (baseline)
  WAL size after writes: 0 bytes
  Meta in main file: PRESENT

Phase 2: Hard kill WITHOUT fix
  WAL size: 0 bytes
  Meta in main file: MISSING (no meta table — data was WAL-only)

Phase 3: Hard kill WITH wal_checkpoint fix
  WAL size: 0 bytes
  Meta in main file: PRESENT
```

**Method:** Each phase creates a fresh WAL-mode SQLite DB, creates schema, inserts a chunk, and writes `memory_index_meta_v1`. After each phase, the main `.sqlite` file is **copied** to an isolated directory (no `-wal` or `-shm` sidecar) and opened read-only — this ensures we read the checkpointed main file, not replayed WAL.

**Phase 2 proves the bug:** after a hard kill without checkpoint, the main DB file has NO `meta` table — the entire schema was WAL-only. On next startup, the manager sees an empty DB, auto-creates it, and declares `"index metadata is missing"`.

**Phase 3 proves the fix:** with `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` after `writeMeta`, the meta row is in the main file and survives the kill.

This corresponds to the production failure path: gateway process killed (OOM, Ctrl-C, power loss) between `writeMeta()` and `closeMemoryDatabase()` → meta lost → `memory_search` returns `"index metadata is missing"` permanently.

## Fix

After writing the meta row, immediately run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. This forces all WAL data to be flushed to the main database file, so the meta row survives even if the process is killed before `closeMemoryDatabase()`.

## What this PR does NOT do

- ❌ No stale file cleanup (belongs in `manager-atomic-reindex.ts` lifecycle — filed as follow-up)
- ❌ No changes to the atomic reindex swap protocol
- ❌ No new dependencies or schema migrations

## Related issues

- #90361 — Canonical bug: intermittent "index metadata is missing"
- #90650 — CLI works but agent tool fails
- #91497 — Meta not written during --force reindex
- #92187 — OOM during rebuild leaves empty DB

The `needsMissingIdentityReindex` auto-recovery path (already on main) can eventually heal this when the provider is available. This checkpoint fix prevents the meta loss in the first place, avoiding unnecessary full reindex cycles after crashes.

## Testing

- **Spy test**: verifies `writeMeta` calls `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` independently of `closeMemoryDatabase` — this test fails on current main
- **Integration test**: verifies meta durability across manager close/reopen cycles

target.title: fix(heartbeat): inject consumed system event text into heartbeat prompt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99544 (follow-up to #61502). Slack interactive button clicks wake the target session and thread, but the clicked action's `value` never reaches the agent as input. The `consumeSelectedSystemEventEntries` call removes the interaction entry from the system event queue, but the event text was never injected into the heartbeat prompt.

## Root Cause / Fix

The heartbeat runner's prompt resolution has specialized builders for exec-completion and cron events, but the generic fallback path never includes system event text. When a Slack `hook` wake triggers a heartbeat with no exec/cron events, the generic prompt is used and the interaction payload is silently dropped.

**Fix**: Prepend pending system event text to the heartbeat prompt on the generic path, formatted with `System:` event-block semantics (matching `drainFormattedSystemEvents`), guarded by `!hasExecCompletion && !hasCronEvents`.

- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`: Add `System:`-framed injection block before `ctx` construction

target.title: fix(msteams): bound Bot Framework attachmentInfo JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bot Framework personal-chat attachment downloads call `/v3/attachments/{id}` and previously parsed the metadata with unbounded `response.json()`. A hostile or misbehaving endpoint could stream an arbitrarily large JSON body and OOM the gateway process before the attachment view download even starts.

Related open bounded-read work covers MS Teams Graph collection (#98833), Graph upload (#97784), and SSO (#97781), but not the Bot Framework `attachmentInfo` path in `bot-framework.ts`.

Note: Inworld TTS/voices bounded reads are already on `main` (#95416, #98660), so this PR targets the remaining MS Teams gap instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the Bot Framework attachment metadata success path through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper (16 MiB cap, stream cancel on overflow), matching sibling MS Teams Graph/OAuth bounded JSON reads.

The 16 MiB fail-closed cap is intentional: successful Bot Framework metadata responses larger than the shared provider JSON cap now fail as invalid attachment metadata instead of being buffered without a limit. That can reject unusual oversized metadata, but keeps the gateway from accepting unbounded JSON on this shipped attachment path.

## User Impact

No config or API changes. Personal DM / Bot Framework attachment downloads fail closed with a logged warning when attachment metadata JSON exceeds the cap, instead of buffering the full body.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: cap Codex native tool output before replay
target.body:
Closes #99465
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where oversized native Codex tool output could remain large enough in OpenClaw's Codex app-server projection surfaces to dominate replay-bound worker context even though visible transcript rendering had a separate truncation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one shared projector-side cap for native Codex tool output and routes snapshot command output, streamed command-output fallback text, dynamic/MCP projected output text, trajectory `tool.result` output, transcript tool-result messages, and emitted tool-result progress text through it. The cap is `10_000` characters including the truncation notice, and the notice includes the original character count plus the displayed cap.

The change does not claim to fix every future token runaway. It hardens the app-server projection boundary that was still allowing large output text to stay live after a small worker task produced repeated verbose tool results.

## User Impact

Operators and users should see oversized native tool output summarized with an explicit OpenClaw truncation notice instead of having very large command output copied into replay-bound Codex/OpenClaw projection surfaces. This reduces the chance that one verbose command result dominates later worker input tokens.

target.title: feat(google): add typed Gemini CLI auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The original goal is to replace OpenClaw's deprecated `google-gemini-cli` OAuth acquisition flow while keeping the Google auth replacement boundary safe and typed.

There are two supported Google/Gemini cases this PR now models separately:

- `google` API-backed profiles use Gemini API-key credentials.
- `google-gemini-cli` direct Gemini CLI profiles import OAuth credentials created by the official Gemini CLI `Sign in with Google` flow, then stage them into an isolated Gemini CLI auth home for execution.

This avoids launching an OpenClaw-owned Google OAuth browser/callback/token-exchange flow for Gemini CLI auth. OpenClaw no longer scrapes Gemini CLI OAuth client credentials or performs the deprecated `google-gemini-cli` OAuth acquisition process during provider setup.

The PR still keeps the public CLI backend auth-forwarding contract generic, preserves Gemini CLI API-key staging, and makes provider-owned hooks fail closed when they decline forwarding.

## What Changed

- Added official Gemini CLI OAuth cache import support for `google-gemini-cli` setup.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI `oauth_creds.json` cache instead of starting OpenClaw's own Google OAuth flow.
- Added provider-level coverage proving setup imports the official Gemini CLI cache and does not open/log/prompt for an OpenClaw-owned OAuth callback flow.
- Added low-level cache import coverage for `GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`, active Google account import, and project binding from `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`.
- Added a public provider hook, `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`, for provider-owned CLI backend credential resolution.
- Added generic fallback forwarding for standard auth-profile credentials only when the selected provider has no provider-owned hook.
- Made hook absence distinct from hook decline: a registered hook returning `null` or `undefined` blocks forwarding instead of falling through to generic fallback.
- Registered the Gemini CLI OAuth resolver on the bundled `google-gemini-cli` provider.
- Preserved Google API-key fallback forwarding for `google` API-key profiles and Gemini CLI `GEMINI_API_KEY` staging.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after credential resolution.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Made bundled MCP fail closed when loopback startup fails instead of writing a partial config.
- Removed the unused core Google auth resolver and its self-only test; credential resolution now remains provider-owned plus the generic fallback path.
- Updated Google provider docs and docs map so fresh Gemini CLI setup requires official Gemini CLI `Sign in with Google` first and explicitly retires the OpenClaw-owned OAuth client env-var setup path.
- Updated Plugin SDK exports/API baseline and CLI backend plugin docs.
- Updated the proof script so it installs the real Google provider/backend registry, verifies the registered provider hook through runtime lookup, verifies official Gemini CLI cache import, verifies provider setup does not use OpenClaw-owned OAuth, runs `prepareCliRunContext`, and executes the staged Gemini CLI auth-home writes.
- Removed a proof-local SHA-256 recomputation that CodeQL misclassified as a weak password hash; the proof now asserts against `resolveGeminiCliProfileHome(...)` directly.

target.title: fix(feishu): add video preview covers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw sends outbound Feishu videos as `msg_type=media` with only `{ file_key }`. Feishu's message-content docs say video `media` messages can also include an optional `image_key` for the cover image; when OpenClaw omits it, video bubbles can render without a preview frame.

Docs: https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/im-v1/message-content-description/create_json?lang=zh-CN

## Summary
- Generate a JPEG preview frame for outbound Feishu video messages and upload it with the existing image upload API.
- Include the returned `image_key` alongside `file_key` for `msg_type=media`, matching Feishu's documented video content shape.
- Keep the preview best-effort: if frame extraction or preview upload fails, the video still sends with the existing `{ file_key }` payload.
- Bound preview extraction with a short 5s ffmpeg timeout so failed covers do not stall outbound video delivery.

## Evidence
- `git diff --check`
- `/Users/l/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/feishu/src/media.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`

- Live Feishu send with the branch succeeded for a 5-second mp4. A `message.get` readback returned `code=0`, `msgType=media`, and confirmed the sent content contains both `file_key` and `image_key` without logging the private keys.
- Screenshot proof: the lower video bubble renders the generated preview frame; the upper gray bubble is a no-preview comparison. Duration display is intentionally out of scope for this PR and is covered separately by #98235.

![Feishu video preview proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/areslp/openclaw/codex/pr-98458-feishu-preview-proof/pr-evidence/feishu-video-preview-cover.jpg)

- The first live attempt exposed ffmpeg's safe-output `.part` suffix handling; the implementation explicitly uses `-c:v mjpeg -f image2` instead of relying on the output filename extension.

target.title: fix(discord): preserve text after oversized uploads
target.body:
Closes #99021

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord replies that include an attachment can be silently lost when Discord rejects the upload as too large. Before this change, the text caption traveled in the same multipart request as the file, so a 413 upload rejection dropped the text too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord upload limits vary by guild/account, so this keeps the configured media fetch limit unchanged and adds a last-mile fallback at the Discord send boundary. If Discord rejects the upload as too large, OpenClaw now sends a text-only fallback containing the original text plus a visible note that the attachment was skipped; media-only sends get a visible failure note instead of silence.

## User Impact

Users still see the agent's text reply even when an attached file is over Discord's upload limit. Media-only oversized replies now produce an explicit Discord message explaining that the upload was skipped.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts` — PASS, 46 tests.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/send.shared.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts` — PASS.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/discord/src/send.shared.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts` — PASS, 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` — PASS.
- Diff secret scan — PASS.

No live Discord upload was attempted from this checkout; the regression is covered by deterministic REST-boundary tests that simulate Discord returning HTTP 413 for the media request and verify the follow-up text-only message body.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where diagnostic model-call event accounting still copies stream chunks and model-call event bases with object rest/spread on hot paths. Issue #91588 includes field evidence that points at V8 dictionary-mode `CopyDataProperties` work around the diagnostic stream byte-accounting path during long-running Gateway workloads.

Scope boundary: This PR only addresses diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot paths; it does not close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker or prove multi-day RSS plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change removes object rest from `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` and conditional object spreads from `baseModelCallEvent()` while keeping the same diagnostic event fields. The stream copy now uses a null-prototype target so an own enumerable `__proto__` stream-chunk field remains a data key instead of interacting with `Object.prototype` behavior.

This PR is ready for review for the narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation because validation now covers focused regression behavior plus an inspectable synthetic runtime benchmark. Longer-running Gateway RSS proof remains outside this submission's current evidence.

## User Impact

Operators running long-lived Gateway sessions should get less diagnostic hot-path object-copy churn during model-call streaming. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter model responses, provider transport, or persisted session data.

## Breaking changes (if any)

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` on stream chunks with direct JSON byte accounting for own enumerable fields except `partial`, avoiding a snapshotless chunk allocation on the normal non-`toJSON` path while preserving JSON omission behavior for unsupported values.
- Preserve root `JSON.stringify` semantics when a stream chunk exposes callable `toJSON` via own non-enumerable or inherited/prototype lookup: a rare proxy path hides `partial` lazily, and a descriptor-preserving fallback handles non-configurable/non-extensible shapes.
- Keep own enumerable `__proto__` chunk fields as JSON-serializable data keys without mutating `Object.prototype`, including the `toJSON` snapshot fallback path.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally instead of using conditional spread literals.
- Add regression coverage for partial getter safety, callable `toJSON` byte accounting, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key preservation.
## Labels considered

`P0`, `impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`, `impact:crash-loop`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`, and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` from #91588 were considered when setting this PR's narrow scope and draft status.

## Validation

Current PR head: `6e61cec3c548f1f3057b8a478eb6320e3c144232`
Proof baseline commit: `28a841472684eed2d98a1a277fcefc30855b580b`

GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof:

- `PR 99154 model diagnostic runtime proof` — passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28668472036
- Artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28668472036-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions, `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Head binding: artifact `head.json` records `commit=6e61cec3c548f1f3057b8a478eb6320e3c144232`, matching the current PR head.
- Edge behavior:
  - Baseline partial-getter edge failed as expected: `partialReads=1`, no byte count.
  - PR head partial-getter edge passed: `partialReads=0`, `responseStreamBytes=34`.
  - PR head own non-enumerable `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, `partialReads=0`, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`.
  - PR head inherited/prototype `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `35` bytes.
  - PR head non-configurable `partial` snapshot fallback edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
  - PR head own enumerable `__proto__` data-key edge passed: expected/actual `73` bytes, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
- Synthetic model-call stream benchmark:
  - 50000 representative non-delta stream chunks were drained through `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()`.
  - Baseline duration: `171.83 ms`; PR head duration: `170.3 ms` in this run.
  - Baseline and PR head both reported `responseStreamBytes=2911669`, so the diagnostic byte-accounting contract stayed stable.
  - Short-run RSS deltas are recorded in the artifact but are not used as multi-day RSS proof.

GitHub Actions/check read-back on current PR head:

- Passed: `CI` https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28668427957
- Passed: `QA Smoke CI`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-lint`, `check-guards`, `build-artifacts`, extension/package/runtime boundary checks, contract shards, and all node compact shards.
- Passed: `OpenGrep OSS`, `security-fast`, `Workflow Sanity`, `Dependency Guard`, `CodeQL`, `CodeQL Critical Quality`, and `Real behavior proof` according to the current PR status rollup.
- PR status rollup at this update time has no failed or pending checks.

Local pre-check only:

- `git diff --check` — passed with no output before push.
## Evidence source map

- Issue field evidence: #91588 contains public native stack evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection and identifies the diagnostic stream chunk copy site.
- GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28668472036 compares the baseline commit and current PR head with a 50,000-chunk model-call diagnostic stream workload, plus edge checks for partial snapshots, callable `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- Regression tests: `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts` covers partial snapshot exclusion without reading `partial`, own non-enumerable/prototype `toJSON` behavior, non-configurable `partial` fallback, unrelated lazy getters, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key byte accounting.
- GitHub Actions/checks: current-head proof passed and current PR status rollup is green with no failed or pending checks at this update time.
- Local pre-check only: whitespace/diff check listed above.
## Data model / migration compatibility

No persistent data model or runtime storage schema is changed. The only test-file additions exercise diagnostic event byte accounting and do not alter serialized session state, vector/embedding metadata, migrations, or upgrade behavior.

## Risk

- Diagnostic byte accounting can be sensitive to unusual provider stream chunk shapes. The added tests and proof cover the relevant review edges: skipping `partial` without reading it, callable `toJSON` lookup/ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- The proxy branch is intentionally limited to chunks with callable `toJSON`; the normal non-`toJSON` stream path remains allocation-free for snapshotless chunk accounting.
- This does not address diagnostic maps, session retention, plugin retention, or other long-running RSS contributors discussed in #91588.
- The implementation avoids provider/runtime behavior changes and is limited to diagnostic event construction and byte accounting.
## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data migration, config migration, or persisted format change is involved.

## Docs updated

No documentation files were changed. The patch is limited to diagnostic implementation code plus focused regression tests.

## Related issue / PR

- Related: #91588
- Related: #97211

#97211 covers the same diagnostic hot path and has public review feedback around proof, scope, and `__proto__` behavior. This PR carries focused regression tests and uses non-closing issue references so it does not auto-close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker.

## Review context addressed

- ClawSweeper requested inspectable real behavior proof before merge. The PR body now includes the current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof run and artifact listed in Validation.
- ClawSweeper flagged stale proof/head mismatch. The current artifact records `commit=6e61cec3c548f1f3057b8a478eb6320e3c144232`, matching the current PR head.
- Review feedback flagged that the earlier byte counter bypassed callable `toJSON` semantics. The implementation now preserves root `JSON.stringify` callable `toJSON` lookup for own non-enumerable and inherited/prototype methods while hiding `partial`.

target.title: fix: keep OpenClaw control tools available when tool_search misroutes
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation/control tools it needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now keeps the critical control-path dynamic tools, `heartbeat_respond`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`, in the direct Codex tool surface while leaving broad OpenClaw tools deferred/searchable. This preserves Codex-native `spawn_agent` as the recommended Codex-subagent path in developer instructions, but removes the unsafe dependency on a successful deferred search result for OpenClaw/ACP delegation and heartbeat handling.

Codex source inspection for this change used sibling `../codex` at `da4c8ca57d40b074bdc1b5b1218851100150c56b`:

- `codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1557-1566` documents that deferred dynamic functions must be namespaced and are searchable only when `tool_search` is available.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:494-536` enables deferred-tool guidance only when the search tool is enabled.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:964-984` builds `tool_search` only from planned deferred runtimes with search info.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs:74-87` builds the search index from the supplied deferred-tool search infos.

## User Impact

OpenClaw Codex workers keep access to OpenClaw heartbeat and session delegation controls even when deferred `tool_search` is unavailable or returns unrelated connector results. Operators should see fewer fallbacks to expensive raw shell inspection when an OpenClaw worker needs OpenClaw-specific session controls.

target.title: fix(codex): ignore missing mirrored session history
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server harness hooks can warn with `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks` when they read mirrored history before the session JSONL file exists.

Current `main` already treats parsed-empty session history as `[]`, so this PR focuses on the remaining transient state: `ENOENT` while the file-backed active transcript artifact has not been created yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing mirrored session file during startup means there is no history to replay yet. It should behave like empty history rather than surfacing as a failed history read.

Malformed non-empty history remains unchanged: the reader still returns `undefined`, so the existing warning path continues to surface real transcript corruption.

## User Impact

This reduces noisy Codex embedded-runtime warnings for healthy new sessions whose mirrored history file is created after the harness hook runs.

It does not suppress warnings for malformed non-empty transcript files.

## Evidence

- Local gateway log evidence from `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-07-03.log`: `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks` appeared for yuantai cron sessions before the corresponding JSONL file's first record timestamp; after the run completed, those files parsed successfully.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed in the rebased worktree before running validation.
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` live terminal proof passed from the patched checkout and imported the production `runCodexAppServerAttempt` path, not Vitest.
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` live terminal proof passed from the patched checkout and imported the production `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages` wrapper, not Vitest.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history.test.ts` passed with `12` tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Codex harness hook history reads should not warn when the mirrored session file is temporarily missing during a new-session startup race.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw gateway logs from `2026-07-03` under the user's active `~/.openclaw` state, plus the current source checkout rebased onto `upstream/main` at `0420aefb1d` and patched through `fb7c53c51c`.

### After-fix production Codex attempt proof

This proof does not use Vitest. It runs a one-shot Node process from the patched checkout, imports the production `runCodexAppServerAttempt` implementation from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts`, starts an in-process app-server client double, and lets the real Codex attempt startup path proceed through `thread/start`, `turn/start`, and cleanup. The session file is intentionally missing before the attempt starts, matching the startup race that produced the gateway warning.

Exact post-patch command shape:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { embeddedAgentLog } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime';
import { runCodexAppServerAttempt } from './extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts';

// Create a temp workspace with a missing session.jsonl, run the production
// Codex attempt startup path with an in-process app-server client, and count
// whether the exact harness-hook warning is emitted.
EOF
```

Relevant output from the patched checkout:

```text
patched production Codex attempt proof: missing mirrored session.jsonl
  before_run_session_file_exists=no
  after_run_session_file_exists=yes
  app_server_methods=thread/start,turn/start,thread/unsubscribe
  result_keys=aborted,agentHarnessResultClassification,assistantTexts,attemptUsage,bootstrapPromptWarningSignature,bootstrapPromptWarningSignaturesSeen,cloudCodeAssistFormatError,currentAttemptAssistant,didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool,didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt,didSendViaMessagingTool,externalAbort,heartbeatToolResponse,idleTimedOut,itemLifecycle,lastAssistant,messagesSnapshot,messagingToolSentMediaUrls,messagingToolSentTargets,messagingToolSentTexts,messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads,promptError,promptErrorSource,replayMetadata,sessionIdUsed,successfulCronAdds,systemPromptReport,timedOut,timedOutDuringCompaction,timedOutDuringToolExecution,toolAudioAsVoice,toolMediaUrls,toolMetas,yieldDetected
  client_closed=no
  warning="failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks" emitted=no
  total_warn_count=0
```

What the production attempt proof verifies:

- The session JSONL is absent before the attempt starts (`before_run_session_file_exists=no`).
- The same production attempt path used by Codex embedded runtime reaches app-server startup and turn execution (`thread/start`, `turn/start`, `thread/unsubscribe`).
- The exact reported warning is not emitted while the missing session file is treated as empty history.
- The runtime creates the session file later in the turn (`after_run_session_file_exists=yes`), matching the observed startup race rather than a permanently invalid path.

### After-fix production wrapper proof

This proof does not use Vitest. It runs a one-shot Node process from the patched checkout, imports the production `readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages` wrapper from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts`, and captures the production `embeddedAgentLog.warn` call site that emits `failed to read mirrored session history for codex harness hooks`.

Exact post-patch command shape:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { embeddedAgentLog } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime';
import { readMirroredSessionHistoryMessages } from './extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts';

// Create a temp missing session.jsonl, call the production wrapper, and count
// whether the exact harness-hook warning is emitted. Then repeat with a
// malformed non-empty JSONL row to prove the real-corruption warning path stays.
EOF
```

Relevant output from the patched checkout:

